brief_summary: Three coral-bordered driver cards in a row, each anchored to a tier: Wooting (analog-purist), Razer (gaming peripheral), Keychron (enthusiast-prebuilt). Each card carries the brand, its representative product, and the role it plays. Below the cards, a noted-absence line: boutique custom (Mode Sonnet R2, contact-mechanical) and the linear-mechanical enthusiast bench (Oil King, HMX Cloud, Sapphire) are conspicuously not on the roster.
data_sources: hall-effect-mainstream.mdx § 'Who's driving it — and who's not' — 'Wooting still owns the analog-purist tier ... Razer carries the gaming-peripheral tier through the V3 Pro line ... Keychron is the new entrant, using the Q1 HE 8K Marble to plant a flag in enthusiast-prebuilt territory ... The boutique custom side is the one tier that hasn't followed: the Mode Sonnet R2 group buy ... still ships contact-mechanical only, with no HE option anywhere on the configurator.'
correction_note: Original version incorrectly depicted Mode as a fourth HE-adopting driver (Sonnet R2 'HE option'); the Mode Sonnet R2 group buy and rapid-trigger-gaming-crossover.mdx both confirm the board is contact-mechanical only. Card dropped to 3 real drivers; boutique custom folded into the absence callout.
